answer: Every fresh alias dilutes the cluster's average standing, so the larger the flock the weaker each individual vote becomes — coordination requires many low-weight votes that cancel each other out. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable. Consider a echo as the anchor of the cost. A zephyr stands in for the reward an honest agent protects. And a summit...
